title: 07 Isobath Ocean Observatory: climate data hero
strengths: The picture is the institute's own data: bathymetric contours, a float marker with depth, a marine-heatwave label, latitude ticks on the frame edge; nothing decorative
IBM Plex Sans light for the headline and Plex Mono for every number is a disciplined two-face system; one teal, one coral, used only for live state
Readouts carry units and baselines (+1.38 °C vs 1991-2020 mean, 168 µmol/kg, -0.017 per decade) and the status bar says 'DATA CC BY 4.0 · UPDATED 14:06:22 UTC': the page reads as published science
slop_signals: Headline left, four stacked readout cards right, two buttons (filled teal 'Explore live data', underlined 'Read the 2026 Ocean Heat Report'): the SaaS skeleton under the science
Four readout cards of identical height with a sparkline each is close to the 'feature cards with icons' rhythm
'The ocean keeps the record.' is a slogan; the institute's own voice is in the sub-line
fixes: Dock the readouts into the map (labels on the contours) or reduce to two, so the map is the one subject
One button; the report link belongs in the nav or the status bar
Consider the sub-line as the headline: the hourly readings and 6,000 metres are the claim

references.what: One line drawing on dark with a single mono caption; the same restraint our map has, with even less around it
A data-driven globe is the hero and one card is docked on it; live data as the picture
Dark hero with a hairline grid and the product panel bleeding off the edge; small plain buttons
A wireframe sphere on dark with one word; shows the register our contour drawing sits in

changed: The four-card readout rail is gone; one float's profile panel is docked to the float on the map by a short leader (temperature to 2,000 m against the 1991-2020 October mean, the warm 38 m mixed layer in coral, +1.38 C), with three readings shown nowhere else

The map is a real chart: contours every 100 m with exact index labels every 500 m, one positive depth convention, a true graticule with every line labelled, a 50 km scale bar; the radial glow and the crosshair reticle are gone
The warm-water anomaly is its own irregular dashed outline with a plain label, not colour painted onto the sea-floor contours

Headline states the reach ('The North Atlantic, from the surface to 6,000 metres.'), one button, sentence case; data corrected (612 instruments, O2 246 umol/kg, a deep profile that differs from the mean)
Panel aligned to the 64 px margin, the eyebrow's top and the button's bottom; nav underline on the nav rule

facts: The seamount is generated in code, not drawn from real bathymetry (the auditor's reason it stays below 5)

pairwise.note: The final round only moved the 5,000 m label inside the frame and the seamount 40 px left; it was not re-judged after that.

changed: Contours no longer run behind the copy: only the seamount is drawn, off centre to the right, so the copy sits on open sea; the legibility scrim is gone

Removed: the graticule and its latitude and longitude labels, the scale bar, the dashed anomaly ring and its label, the float track, the profile card with its chart, legend and three stat cells, the eyebrow and the coordinates footer
Contours every 200 m with brighter 1,000 m index lines (was every 100 m), two depth labels set along their lines (3,000 m and 5,000 m)
The float's reading sits beside its marker in two lines, lettered with a halo in the sea's colour instead of a box: 'Surfaced 13:52 UTC · +1.38 °C above the October mean'
The button is an outline, so teal means depth and coral means warm water
